- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation — add 2–5% to forecast mean.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — delay forecast shift by 1–2 periods.
- If model forecast mean is > 10% above true outcome mean over 30d, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1.5–3% from forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.20 → -0.40 → +0.20), model overfits short-term sentiment — dampen forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion to 65–68 range after 10+ days of volatility, model often overestimates — cap forecast at 68–70.
